brief: A narrated 60-second explainer on how vaccines train the immune system, with sources.
requirements: Narrated: continuous spoken narration with a real audio stream in the mix
Language: narration and on-screen text in English (the request's language)

Content: explains HOW vaccines train the immune system - the mechanism (a vaccine presents a harmless form of an antigen; the immune system responds and builds antibodies plus memory cells that remember it) - not a vague 'vaccines work'
'With sources': every factual claim (numbers, names, causal statements) has a facts entry - source URL, quote found in the stored snapshot, verified offline
Sources are real, authoritative health references (e.g. WHO, CDC, a national health service), snapshotted - no invented citations
Unverifiable claims are hedged or cut - never guessed
The claims are biology, not algebra: they are sourced facts or hedges, never presented as sympy-verified proofs
No format is named in the brief: the plan states its assumed format (e.g. 16:9) as an explicit assumption and delivers exactly that
One audio mix at the studio loudness target (narration intelligible: LUFS within 1, true peak <= -1 dBTP)
must_not: must not present biological claims as sympy proofs (the claims ledger verifies algebra; vaccine facts need sources or hedges)
must not ship an unsourced claim ('with sources' is the ask: sourced, hedged or cut)
must not invent citations (sources are real pages, snapshotted, the quote found in the snapshot)
must not pick a technique that cannot narrate (plain motion has no voice of its own - narration is an explicit ask)
must not switch language (the request is English)
must not drift from the 60 seconds
must not invent inputs (no footage or files are needed; none may be flagged or fabricated)
